id.description: Dropped on a COMPACTED merchant listing row (§3.13): a catalog names the item to buy by index, and the listing's own id is what a purchase acts on. Present everywhere else, and restored by --full.

effects.description: §3.12 (enrich): what USE and EQUIP allocate, one row per raw allo — the "is this useful to me?" facts, on the row that holds the item.

requirements.description: §3.12 (enrich): what USE requires. Empty array = the registry stores no USE condition.

for.description: §3.13 (0.5.0): who the item is FOR — KAMI / ACCOUNT / …. The single fact that tells a kami food from an account food when both read `type: FOOD` (one merchant catalog at this pin sells "Maple-Flavor Ghost Gum" for KAMI beside "Ice Cream" for ACCOUNT). OMITTED, not served as an empty string, when the world holds no target: 77 of 177 items genuinely have none.

rarity.description: §3.13 (0.5.0): the rarity the reference client's item tooltip renders.

disabled.description: §3.13 (0.5.0): present and true only when the registry marks the item disabled — the reference client titles such an item "Name (disabled)".

AlloText.description: The pinned client's own interpretation of one allocation, projected to {name, description}. `image` is never served: two shapes files carry the module NAMESPACE of a png import there rather than a URL (SPEC §4.1 quirk 2).

AlloOut.description: One RAW allocation the world stores (type, index, value) with the pinned client's interpretation of it beside it. Grouped per raw allo deliberately: the interpreter fans out — a BONUS allo yields one entry per bonus, a droptable allo one consolidated entry — so a flat parsed list would have no positional correspondence to what the world holds. `entries` is empty when this pin interprets the shape not at all; the raw facts still stand.

ItemRequirement.description: One USE requirement: the raw condition target plus the pinned client's interpreted text. Grouped rather than a bare string because 48 of the 53 item conditions at this pin are KAMI_CAN_EAT with index 0, whose text is the single word "None" — indistinguishable, without the target beside it, from a real requirement. Text is verbatim, upstream spacing quirks included.
